pubchem-947.cite: PubChem CID 947, Nitrogen (record description and Use and Manufacturing sections).
pubchem-947.checked: 2026-10-01 (PUG REST description, PUG View Uses): dinitrogen, an elemental molecule of two nitrogen atoms; role as a food packaging gas (ChEBI).

pubchem-977.cite: PubChem CID 977, Oxygen (record description and Use and Manufacturing sections).
pubchem-977.checked: 2026-10-01 (PUG REST description, PUG View Uses): dioxygen, a gas molecular entity and diatomic oxygen (ChEBI).

pubchem-280.cite: PubChem CID 280, Carbon Dioxide (record description and Use and Manufacturing sections).
pubchem-280.checked: 2026-10-01 (PUG REST description, PUG View Uses): carbon attached to each oxygen by a double bond; colourless, odourless gas; produced during respiration by all animals, fungi and microorganisms that depend on living or decaying plants for food; member of greenhouse gas (ChEBI).

pubchem-23968.cite: PubChem CID 23968, Argon (record description and Use and Manufacturing sections).
pubchem-23968.checked: 2026-10-01 (PUG REST description, PUG View Uses): argon(0) is a monoatomic argon (ChEBI).

pubchem-24823.cite: PubChem CID 24823, Ozone (record description and Use and Manufacturing sections).
pubchem-24823.checked: 2026-10-01 (PUG REST description, PUG View Uses): elemental molecule O3; pale blue gas with a pungent odour, continuously produced in the upper atmosphere by solar ultraviolet radiation acting on oxygen; used as an antimicrobial agent and disinfectant (ChEBI, HSDB).

pubchem-5234.cite: PubChem CID 5234, Sodium Chloride (record description and Use and Manufacturing sections).
pubchem-5234.checked: 2026-10-01 (PUG REST description, PUG View Uses): inorganic chloride salt with sodium(1+) as counterion (ChEBI); used for food flavouring; produced from salt mines or by evaporating seawater or mineral-rich spring water (T3DB).

pubchem-176.cite: PubChem CID 176, Acetic Acid (record description and Use and Manufacturing sections).
pubchem-176.checked: 2026-10-01 (PUG REST description, PUG View Uses): simple monocarboxylic acid containing two carbons; food acidity regulator and antimicrobial food preservative (ChEBI); gives vinegar its sour taste and pungent smell (Uses).

pubchem-311.cite: PubChem CID 311, Citric Acid (record description and Use and Manufacturing sections).
pubchem-311.checked: 2026-10-01 (PUG REST description, PUG View Uses): a compound from citrus fruits that is an intermediate in the tricarboxylic acid (Krebs) cycle, used as an acidifying agent in foods, beverages and pharmaceuticals (Dorland via ChemIDplus); important metabolite in the pathway of all aerobic organisms; propane-1,2,3-tricarboxylic acid with a hydroxy group at position 2 (ChEBI).

pubchem-516892.cite: PubChem CID 516892, Sodium Bicarbonate (record description and Use and Manufacturing sections).
pubchem-516892.checked: 2026-10-01 (PUG REST description, PUG View Uses): organic sodium salt containing a hydrogencarbonate; role as an antacid (ChEBI); source of carbon dioxide, ingredient of baking powder (HSDB); JECFA classes leavening agent and raising agent.

pubchem-702.cite: PubChem CID 702, Ethanol (record description and Use and Manufacturing sections).
pubchem-702.checked: 2026-10-01 (PUG REST description, PUG View Uses): ethane with one hydrogen replaced by a hydroxy group (ChEBI); primary ingredient in alcoholic beverages and used as a topical disinfectant for its bactericidal activity (ChemIDplus); solvent in household products and pharmaceuticals; octane booster in gasoline and a fuel (HSDB).

pubchem-1183.cite: PubChem CID 1183, Vanillin (record description and Use and Manufacturing sections).
pubchem-1183.checked: 2026-10-01 (PUG REST description, PUG View Uses): benzaldehyde with methoxy and hydroxy groups at positions 3 and 4, flavouring agent (ChEBI); flavouring agent in confectionery, beverages and foods (Merck Index); major commercial source of natural vanillin is vanilla bean extract, also occurs in orchids and clove bud oil (HSDB, Natural occurrence).

pubchem-313.cite: PubChem CID 313, Hydrochloric Acid (record description and Use and Manufacturing sections).
pubchem-313.checked: 2026-10-01 (PUG REST description, PUG View Uses): hydrochloric acid is found naturally in gastric acid; most hydrogen chloride gas is used to make hydrochloric acid (T3DB, Uses).

pubchem-222.cite: PubChem CID 222, Ammonia (record description and Use and Manufacturing sections).
pubchem-222.checked: 2026-10-01 (PUG REST description, PUG View Uses): one nitrogen atom covalently bonded to three hydrogen atoms, a gas (ChEBI); about 80 percent is used in fertilizers (ATSDR); used directly on farm crops and found in many household and industrial cleaners (Uses).

pubchem-784.cite: PubChem CID 784, Hydrogen Peroxide (record description and Use and Manufacturing sections).
pubchem-784.checked: 2026-10-01 (PUG REST description, PUG View Uses): used for bleaching and disinfecting, including in hairdressing (ACGIH via Haz-Map); used in antiseptics and to bleach hair (HSDB).

pubchem-297.cite: PubChem CID 297, Methane (record description and Use and Manufacturing sections).
pubchem-297.checked: 2026-10-01 (PUG REST description, PUG View Uses): carbon attached by single bonds to four hydrogen atoms; colourless, odourless, non-toxic but flammable gas; fossil fuel and greenhouse gas (ChEBI); major component of natural gas, piped into homes for heating and cooking (T3DB).

pubchem-6334.cite: PubChem CID 6334, Propane (record description and Use and Manufacturing sections).
pubchem-6334.checked: 2026-10-01 (PUG REST description, PUG View Uses): gas molecular entity and alkane (ChEBI); used as a fuel, solvent, refrigerant and propellant (Hawley); component of liquid petroleum gas; household and industrial fuel; aerosol propellant (HSDB).

pubchem-2724691.cite: PubChem CID 2724691, Sodium Stearate (record description and Use and Manufacturing sections).
pubchem-2724691.checked: 2026-10-01 (PUG REST description, PUG View Uses): organic sodium salt of equal numbers of sodium and stearate ions, role as a detergent (ChEBI); most common ingredient in soap (CHEMINFO).

pubchem-5281.cite: PubChem CID 5281, Stearic Acid (record description and Use and Manufacturing sections).
pubchem-5281.checked: 2026-10-01 (PUG REST description, PUG View Uses): C18 straight-chain saturated fatty acid found in many animal and vegetable lipids; used in hardening soaps (ChEBI).

pubchem-2244.cite: PubChem CID 2244, Aspirin (record description and Use and Manufacturing sections).
pubchem-2244.checked: 2026-10-01 (PUG REST description, PUG View Uses): acetylsalicylic acid, a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug with cyclooxygenase inhibitor activity (ChEBI); relieves pain, reduces fever and prevents blood from clotting quickly; not recommended for children because of a link to Reye syndrome, a serious liver disease (Consumer Product Information Database).

pubchem-16666.cite: PubChem CID 16666, (-)-Menthol (record description and Use and Manufacturing sections).
pubchem-16666.checked: 2026-10-01 (PUG REST description, PUG View Uses): (1R,2S,5R) stereochemistry, the most common naturally occurring enantiomer (ChEBI); found in peppermint oil and other mint oils, used as a flavour in confectionery, cough drops and nasal inhalers and as a topical antipruritic (Merck Index); primarily activates the cold-sensitive TRPM8 receptors in the skin, causing a feeling of coolness (Pharmacology).

osc-2-6.cite: OpenStax Chemistry 2e, section 2.6 Ionic and Molecular Compounds.
osc-2-6.checked: 2026-10-01: compounds are ionic or molecular; a sodium cation has lost an electron; each sodium atom gives up one electron and each chlorine atom accepts one, so NaCl has one Na+ for each Cl-; ionic bonds are electrostatic attractions between ions of opposite charge; an ionic compound is not made of discrete molecules; sodium chloride melts at 801 C while water melts at 0 C; H2O2, the bleach and disinfectant, is molecular (Example 2.12).

osc-10-6.cite: OpenStax Chemistry 2e, section 10.6 Lattice Structures in Crystalline Solids.
osc-10-6.checked: 2026-10-01: NaCl: Na+ and Cl- radii 102 pm and 181 pm; all octahedral holes filled; an octahedral hole is at the centre of six anions; the unit cell holds four sodium and four chloride ions; anions much larger than cations, such as NaCl, usually form an FCC structure.

osc-11-5.checked: 2026-10-01: salts of fatty acids are called soaps; sodium stearate, C17H35CO2Na, has an uncharged nonpolar hydrocarbon chain and an ionic carboxylate group; the hydrocarbon end dissolves in or is attracted to oil, grease or dirt; the ionic end is attracted by water; soap acts as a bridge between nonpolar and polar matter and emulsifies oil drops in water.

osc-14-1.cite: OpenStax Chemistry 2e, section 14.1 Bronsted-Lowry Acids and Bases.
osc-14-1.checked: 2026-10-01: a compound that donates a proton is a Bronsted-Lowry acid and one that accepts a proton is a base; an acid-base reaction is the transfer of a proton; ammonia accepts a proton from water and becomes ammonium ion.

osc-14-2.cite: OpenStax Chemistry 2e, section 14.2 pH and pOH.
osc-14-2.checked: 2026-10-01: at 25 C acidic pH < 7, neutral pH = 7, basic pH > 7; Figure 14.3: gastric juices about pH 1.5, lime juice about 2, pure water 7, household ammonia just under 12; Example 14.4 treats stomach acid as a solution of HCl.

osc-14-3.cite: OpenStax Chemistry 2e, section 14.3 Relative Strengths of Acids and Bases.
osc-14-3.checked: 2026-10-01: acetic acid is the principal ingredient in vinegar and provides its sour taste; vinegar contains acetic acid, a weak acid (Figure 14.9); strong acids such as hydrogen chloride are completely ionized in water, weak acids only partly (Figure 14.6, 14.7); hydrogen carbonate ion appears among the bases.

osc-18-9.cite: OpenStax Chemistry 2e, section 18.9 Occurrence, Preparation, and Compounds of Oxygen.
osc-18-9.checked: 2026-10-01: oxygen occurs as O2 and, to a limited extent, O3 in air; ozone forms in the upper atmosphere by ultraviolet light on oxygen; most atmospheric ozone is in the stratosphere, about 10 to 50 km up, where it absorbs harmful ultraviolet light; stratospheric ozone decreases the frequency of skin cancer; the bent O3 molecule (Figure 18.42); ozone has a distinctive, sharp odour; photosynthesis turns carbon dioxide and water into glucose and oxygen and replenishes atmospheric oxygen.

osc-18-12.cite: OpenStax Chemistry 2e, section 18.12 Occurrence, Preparation, and Properties of the Noble Gases.
osc-18-12.checked: 2026-10-01: noble gases were assumed nonreactive because they have filled valence shells; argon is the third most abundant gas in dry air and comes from fractional distillation of liquid air; argon was used in gas-filled light bulbs to slow the vaporization of the tungsten filament.

osc-20-1.checked: 2026-10-01: methane, CH4, is the principal component of natural gas; hydrocarbons are used every day as fuels such as natural gas and propane; Table 20.1: propane C3H8 is a gas at STP, boiling point -42.1 C.

osap-23-4.cite: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, section 23.4 The Stomach.
osap-23-4.checked: 2026-10-01: parietal cells produce hydrochloric acid; HCl gives the stomach contents a pH of 1.5 to 3.5 and is needed to activate pepsin, the protein-digesting enzyme; mucus bicarbonate ions neutralize acid.

nasa-earthfact.cite: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center, Earth Fact Sheet (atmospheric composition).
nasa-earthfact.checked: 2026-10-01: dry air by volume: nitrogen 78.08 percent, oxygen 20.95 percent, argon 9340 ppm, carbon dioxide 420 ppm, neon 18.18 ppm, helium 5.24 ppm, methane 1.94 ppm; water highly variable, typically about 1 percent.

noaa-co2.cite: NOAA Global Monitoring Laboratory, global annual mean carbon dioxide (co2_annmean_gl.txt).
noaa-co2.checked: 2026-10-01: 2025 global annual mean 425.62 ppm (mole fraction in dry air); the yearly mean rises every year from 1979 (336.85) to 2025.

eia-natgas.cite: US Energy Information Administration, Natural gas explained.
eia-natgas.checked: 2026-10-01: the largest component of natural gas is methane, one carbon atom and four hydrogen atoms (CH4).

epa-methane.cite: US Environmental Protection Agency, Importance of Methane (Global Methane Initiative).
epa-methane.checked: 2026-10-01: methane is more than 28 times as potent as carbon dioxide at trapping heat; the largest US human sources are oil and gas systems, livestock enteric fermentation and landfills.
